updateCadence: Roughly yearly (3.2.0 in Jan 2025, 3.3.0 in Apr 2026)
summary: Dillo is a small graphical browser written in C++ on FLTK. It has no JavaScript and handles only a subset of CSS, but starts instantly and runs on very old hardware. Version 3.3.0 arrived in April 2026.
bestFor: Minimalists who want no JavaScript at all
notFor: Modern web apps, logins and video
People who need an audited, sandboxed browser

pros.title: Extremely light
pros.detail: Fast start and a tiny memory footprint.

pros.title: No JavaScript
pros.detail: Removes a large part of tracking and attack surface.

pros.title: Recent releases
pros.detail: 3.2.0 (Jan 2025) added WebP and SVG; 3.3.0 (Apr 2026) adds experimental FLTK 1.4 support.

pros.title: Configurable
pros.detail: Options such as link actions, new tab page and image-format ignoring.

cons.title: Breaks most modern sites
cons.detail: No JavaScript and partial CSS support.

cons.title: No sandbox
cons.detail: A C/C++ program with a memory-safety bug history, including a TLS use-after-free fixed in 3.2.0.

cons.title: Domain warning
cons.detail: dillo.org is no longer controlled by the developers; the real site is dillo-browser.org.

faq.a: dillo-browser.org. The old dillo.org domain has not been under the developers’ control since December 2023.
It adds new features, configuration options and fixes, and is the first release with experimental FLTK 1.4 support.

timeline.event: Version 3.2.0: WebP, basic SVG, new CSS units, zoom

switching.note: No importers; bookmarks are a local file.

spec.codecs: Images only (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, basic SVG)

securityHardening: No sandbox; C/C++ with memory-safety fixes
patchSpeed: Small project with roughly yearly releases

featureNotes.adBlocker: No JS; image and URL filtering rules
